title: The spectral gap of a projection scan is at most its modified gap, which is at most the square root of n times the gap
source_title: Spectral independence, coupling and mixing times of projection scans

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line

standard_prerequisites.name: Projection scan
standard_prerequisites.statement: A projection scan is a product of transition matrices, one for each coordinate, applied in a fixed order; P = P_n ... P_1 is the transition matrix of the systematic scan.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the transition matrix whose gaps are compared.

standard_prerequisites.name: Spectral gap and modified gap
standard_prerequisites.statement: The gap gamma of P is one minus the second largest eigenvalue in modulus, and the modified gap is the analogous quantity for the Dirichlet form of a single coordinate transition.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two quantities appearing in the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dirichlet form
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a reversible chain with stationary measure pi, the Dirichlet form of a function is the average of the squared differences weighted by the edge conductances.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity used to compare the two gaps.

core_obligations: Show that the first inequality holds for an arbitrary transition matrix, by using the reverse triangle inequality on a mean-zero unit variance test function to relate the quadratic form of the product to the gap of a single factor (source lines 404-410).

Show the second inequality by expressing the modified gap through the Dirichlet form of a single coordinate step and bounding it by the square root of n times the gap of the full scan (source lines 411-433).

proof_roadmap.step: General first inequality through a test function and the reverse triangle inequality.
Relate the modified gap to the Dirichlet form and bound it by the square root of n times the gap.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 396-402: for a finite product space with a projection scan whose transition matrix is the product of the coordinate matrices, the spectral gap is at most the modified gap, which is at most the square root of n times the spectral gap. The proof (source lines 403-433) has two parts of different kinds: the first inequality is obtained by testing the quadratic form on a mean-zero unit-variance function and applying the reverse triangle inequality, which isolates one factor of the product, while the second is a comparison of the modified gap with the Dirichlet form of a single coordinate step, where the square root of the number of coordinates appears. The statement records neither the test-function step nor the Dirichlet-form computation.
